questions.prompt: Pope St. Pius X's 1907 encyclical Pascendi Dominici Gregis condemned 'Modernism' chiefly for treating doctrine as:
choices: Evolving human religious experience, not unchanging revealed truth
A set of rules with no theological meaning
Something only bishops need to understand
A purely private, invisible matter with no public claims
questions.correctAnswer: Evolving human religious experience, not unchanging revealed truth
questions.explanation: Modernism treated dogma as a symbolic expression of inner religious feeling that shifts with each age, rather than truth revealed once for all. Pius X called it the 'synthesis of all heresies' for how broadly it touched Catholic teaching.
questions.hint: This error makes doctrine follow human feeling instead of the other way around.

citations.reference: Pascendi Dominici Gregis, Pope St. Pius X (1907)
citations.quote: we should define it to be the synthesis of all heresies.

questions.prompt: True or False: 'Americanism,' addressed by Pope Leo XIII in 1899, involved concerns that some were downplaying the Church's supernatural guidance in favor of purely natural virtues and individual initiative.
questions.explanation: Leo XIII's letter Testem Benevolentiae Nostrae warned against minimizing the role of the Church's guidance and supernatural virtues in favor of an overly individualistic, activist spirituality.
questions.hint: The concern was about relying too much on natural human effort and too little on the Church's supernatural help.

citations.reference: Testem Benevolentiae Nostrae, Pope Leo XIII (1899)
citations.quote: we are not able to give approval to those views which, in their collective sense, are called by some 'Americanism.'

questions.prompt: Pius X called Modernism 'the synthesis of all heresies.' What did he mean by this striking phrase?

questions.correctAnswer: That Modernism's own core method could, in principle, reopen and unravel every earlier settled question this topic has covered
questions.explanation: This is a real, serious claim about Modernism's own structure, not simple rhetoric -- if doctrine is fundamentally just evolving religious feeling, then Nicaea's own settled teaching on Christ, Trent's own settled teaching on grace, and every other question this whole topic has traced become, in principle, equally open to revision.

questions.prompt: The Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith's 1984 instruction on liberation theology chiefly warned against:
choices: Uncritically adopting Marxist class-struggle analysis into the Gospel
Any concern at all for the material needs of the poor
Reading and studying the Gospels within a Latin American context
Praying publicly and often for greater social justice
questions.correctAnswer: Uncritically adopting Marxist class-struggle analysis into the Gospel
questions.explanation: Libertatis Nuntius did not condemn concern for the poor -- it warned against theologies that borrowed Marxist analysis wholesale, reducing salvation to political liberation and class conflict.
questions.hint: The concern was about borrowing a specific political ideology's framework, not about caring for the poor.

citations.reference: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, Libertatis Nuntius (1984)
citations.quote: It is difficult, and perhaps impossible, to purify these borrowed concepts of an ideological inspiration which is compatible with Christian faith.

questions.prompt: True or False: The CDF's 1986 follow-up instruction, Libertatis Conscientia, rejected the entire project of connecting Christian faith to concern for the poor and social justice.
questions.explanation: Libertatis Conscientia, issued two years after Libertatis Nuntius, affirmed an authentic theology of liberation grounded in freedom in Christ and the Church's social teaching, while maintaining the earlier document's caution against reducing that liberation to a political ideology.
questions.hint: This is the second of a pair of documents on the same topic, two years apart, already covered in Church History's own final levels.

citations.reference: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, Libertatis Conscientia (1986)
citations.quote: 'The truth will make you free' (Jn 8:32) must enlighten and guide all theological reflection and pastoral decisions in this area.
